global: Let the bards sing that {troop_count} spears marched under my banner this morning, and not one of them faltered.
I count my coffers at {gold} and find them lighter than my pride, friend. Pray I do not spend it on a grander hall.
Ser, the mud of {fief} still clings to my boots, yet the banners of my house now fly over its walls by my own hand.
Weary I am of the endless praise, though it is hardly a burden to hear that {troop_count} of my men held the bridge at dawn.
Whoever dares say my treasury is empty should visit the vaults of my house. {gold} lies there, and I have sworn it shall grow.
What is a victory but a debt paid to the ancestors? I have paid mine in full at {fief}, and sleep the better for it.
Some lords count their rivals' shields. I count only my own, and they number {troop_count} this night.
A small matter, friend: I laughed when the scouts counted my {troop_count} lancers twice, for even the crows could not keep pace.
Let every lord who eyes {fief} remember the thunder of {troop_count} hooves. I shall be waiting, and the road is not kind.
Our {gold} built the walls of {fief}, and every stone was laid with honour. Let no one call that spending vain.
